newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan construction firms hold massive debts-survey.
newsitem.headline: Japan construction firms hold massive debts-survey.

text.p: Outstanding interest-carrying debts held by Japanese construction companies remain at a high level of more than 10 trillion yen, a private credit research company said on Wednesday.

According to a survey of 118 Japanese construction firms by Teikoku Databank Ltd, total outstanding interest-carrying debts stood at 10.3 trillion yen in the financial year which ended on March 31, down a scant 1.7 percent from a year earlier.
"It is obvious that that general contractors' earnings will worsen once Japan moves into a phase of credit-tightening," the leading credit research firm said in the survey.
Teikoku Data stressed that it was "urgent" that the contractors slash their interest-bearing debts, as the profitability of their projects has been worsening and public spending has peaked.
Among the firms surveyed, Kajima Corp 1812 T had the biggest amount of interest-carrying debt, totalling 684.3 billion yen in 1996/97, though it was down 6.7 percent from a year earlier.
Fujita Corp was second with total debt of 637.48 billion yen, down 1.4 percent from a year earlier, followed by Taisei Corp's 616.3 billion yen and Kumagai Gumi Co Ltd's 610.8 billion yen.
Haseko Corp and Tokai Kogyo Co Ltd had debts worth more than their annual sales for the year, while Aoki Corp's debt accounted for about 96 precent of its annual sales, the survey showed.
